conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER: The one candidate, Executive Order 13316's revocation of 'Sections 5 through 7', is accepted as the formal disposition of the fourteen Advisory Committee clauses; their first end is the Committee's own-terms end on 2003-01-11 (Section 7(f) as amended). Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 are not within that revocation, so the order stays YES.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13111 (64 FR 2793, January 15, 1999) created a Task Force on Federal Training Technology (Sections 1 to 4) and an Advisory Committee on Expanding Training Opportunities (Sections 5 to 7), with definitions and a no-rights clause (Sections 8 and 9). Section 7(f) ended the Committee two years after the order; Executive Order 13188 moved that date to January 11, 2003; Executive Order 13218 rewrote Section 6; Executive Order 13316, effective September 30, 2003, revoked Sections 5 to 7 as part of a clean-up of committees that had terminated or whose work was completed. The held U.S. Code note prints the order with Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 still in text. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or sets an end for those sections, and the deadlines in them are not ends. The order is therefore claimed as in force on 2026-10-14 as to Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9, with Sections 5 to 7 ended with the Committee.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test for Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9: no own-terms end exists (the 18-month and six-month periods in Section 2 and the 30-day period in Section 1(b) are performance deadlines, not ends), and the only held later instruments that touch the order are Executive Orders 13188, 13218 and 13316, all of which concern the Advisory Committee in Sections 5 to 7. Executive Order 13316 revokes 'Sections 5 through 7' only.
Current basis: Current predicate: the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 4103 (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) prints Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 as the order's text, marks Sections 5 to 7 as revoked, and shows no revocation of the rest; the bounded searches current-law:usc (1 hit, that note), current-law:ecfr (0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (6 hits, the amendments and the partial revocation) found no ending of Sections 1 to 4, 8 or 9.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Sections 5 to 7 (the Advisory Committee): the Committee's own term ended on January 11, 2003 under Section 7(f) as amended by Executive Order 13188 (held text: the amendment replaces 'two years from the date of the order' with 'on January 11, 2003'). The order allows extension by the President before that date; no held instrument extends it (the number search of held texts, the Code note's complete amendment list of 13188, 13218 and 13316, and the later-events:ofr_catalog search show none), and Executive Order 13316 recites that the committees whose orders it revokes 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The cleanup revocation by Executive Order 13316 (effective September 30, 2003, section 6) is the formal disposition, not the first end. The absence of a held extension is a search result, not proof; if an extension exists the end would fall between January 11 and September 30, 2003. The record date is the stated termination day, January 11, 2003 (inclusive reading; the exclusive reading would end the Committee as that day begins).","independent_command_check":"Section 3 (agency duties) and Section 4 (OPM, Labor and Defense duties) command the named agencies independently of the Task Force's life; Section 8 definitions serve those sections. The Committee clauses depend on the Committee and ended with it.","savings_check":"Advice given by the Committee before it ended is a historical fact, not a continuing command. No savings clause exists in the order's text for Sections 5 to 7.","scope_check":"Forty-nine machine-inventoried clauses cover Sections 1 to 9 and every lettered or numbered paragraph. Deadline clauses (Sections 1(b), 2(a) and 2(b)) are kept operative: a deadline is not an end, and no held source shows the designations, policy or options were performed, so the claim does not assert performance."}

savings.reason: Anything the Advisory Committee produced while it existed is an accrued effect of Sections 5 to 7; Executive Order 13316 revoked those sections and left Sections 1 to 4, 8 and 9 in place.
